t:
(a) None of the funds appropriated in this Act are available to establish a new Department of Defense (department) federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), either as a new entity, or as a separate entity administrated by an organization managing another FFRDC, or as a nonprofit membership corporation consisting of a consortium of other FFRDCs and other nonprofit entities. 
    (b) No member of a Board of Directors, Trustees, Overseers, Advisory Group, Special Issues Panel, Visiting Committee, or any similar entity of a defense FFRDC, and no paid consultant to any defense FFRDC, except when acting in a technical advisory capacity, may be compensated for his or her services as a member of such entity, or as a paid consultant by more than one FFRDC in a fiscal year:  Provided, That a member of any such entity referred to previously in this subsection shall be allowed travel expenses and per diem as authorized under the Federal Joint Travel Regulations, when engaged in the performance of membership duties. 
    (c) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, none of the funds available to the department from any source during fiscal year 2013 may be used by a defense FFRDC, through a fee or other payment mechanism, for construction of new buildings, for payment of cost sharing for projects funded by Government grants, for absorption of contract overruns, or for certain charitable contributions, not to include employee participation in community service and/or development. 
    (d) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, of the funds available to the department during fiscal year 2013, not more than 5,750 staff years of technical effort (staff years) may be funded for defense FFRDCs:  Provided; That of the specific amount referred to previously in this subsection, not more than 1,125 staff years may be funded for the defense studies and analysis FFRDCs:  Provided further, That this subsection shall not apply to staff years funded in the National Intelligence Program (NIP) and the Military Intelligence Program (MIP). 
    (e) The Secretary of Defense shall, with the submission of the department’s fiscal year 2014 budget request, submit a report presenting the specific amounts of staff years of technical effort to be allocated for each defense FFRDC during that fiscal year and the associated budget estimates.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the references to an "Advisory Group", "Special Issues Panel" and "employee participation in community service" signal outside participation. But these are internal governance bodies of FFRDCs whose members' compensation is being capped; the section does not create or require any advisory body to be consulted on a federal decision. The rest is funding limits, staff-year caps and a budget report to Congress, which stays inside the federal government. There is no comment period, hearing, rulemaking, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: No member of a Board of Directors, Trustees, Overseers, Advisory Group, Special Issues Panel, Visiting Committee, or any similar entity of a defense FFRDC

opus.w: The section limits funding and pay for defense FFRDCs. It does not require or allow any federal decision-maker to consult outside parties before acting. The advisory boards mentioned belong to the FFRDCs, and the text only caps their members' compensation, so no outsider is brought into a federal decision. The report in (e) goes to Congress with the budget request, which is inside the government, and 'employee participation in community service' is only a matching keyword.

1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** Subsection (b) names a "Board of Directors, Trustees, Overseers, Advisory Group" and mentions "per diem." That looks like Example 8, where per-diem commission members counted as outside advisors. But these are the FFRDCs' own internal governing bodies. The section only limits how their members are paid. It does not ask any federal official to consult them before deciding anything. Two other traps also fail: the phrase "employee participation in community service" is just a keyword match, and the report in (e) goes to Congress as part of the budget submission, which stays inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section primarily imposes funding restrictions and reporting requirements on the Department of Defense and its Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs). Subsection (e) requires a report to Congress, which is an internal government action. Subsection (b) mentions advisory groups but only to limit their compensation, not to mandate their consultation in a decision-making process. Subsection (c) mentions 'employee participation' in community service, which is internal and not relevant to the definition of public participation in federal decisions. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with outside entities (states, tribes, public, etc.) before making a decision.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "employee participation in community service" in subsection (c) constitutes participation. However, this refers to internal employee activities (volunteering), not external parties participating in federal decision-making. Another tempting reading is that the "Board of Directors... Advisory Group" mentioned in subsection (b) implies participation. However, subsection (b) only regulates compensation for these members; it does not establish the boards or require their input into a specific federal decision within this text. The text is primarily about funding restrictions and reporting requirements. The report in (e) is to Congress (inside government). The restrictions in (a), (c), and (d) are internal budgetary controls. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties before making a decision.
